description: Mentioning a teammate in the browser is effectively impossible. Handles are UUID-like (human-524f986e-…), appear nowhere in the UI (profile dialog, avatar stack, You dialog), and @Name or @name only produces 'matches no Actor'. The only source is `pardner client show` JSON.
expected: Typing @ offers autocomplete by display name, or profiles show a copyable handle, or display-name mentions resolve.
actual: The hint says '@Priya matches no Actor and won't notify anyone.' with no suggestion; the user must use the CLI.
suggested_fix: Add @-autocomplete over project Actors (display name to handle), and include a 'did you mean Priya Raman?' suggestion in the hint.

description: A resolved mention chip shows the raw handle '@human-524f986e-15f9-4996-a464-a2acaa56f3cf'. The person's name appears only in the hover title 'Notified Priya Raman · human'. At 390px the chip breaks mid-handle across two lines.
expected: The chip reads '@Priya Raman', with the handle in the tooltip, and does not wrap.
actual: A UUID chip, and the name only on hover.
suggested_fix: Render the Actor display name in the chip text; keep white-space: nowrap.

description: The server creates a mention for 'ops@human-…' (email-local position), while the UI shows no hint and no chip, so a delivery is created with no visible sign.
expected: The UI and server agree: either both treat it as a mention (chip shown) or neither does.
actual: A mention record exists for Priya, and the comment renders as plain text.
suggested_fix: Apply the same email-local exclusion in mentionedActors on the server (or drop it in the UI).

description: The unknown-handle hint fires for handles inside inline code ('`@priya`'), though chips skip code spans.
expected: No hint for handles inside code.
suggested_fix: Reuse the chip renderer's SKIP rules in unmatchedHandles.
